Our previous interview: https://www.cruxinvestor.com/posts/almadex-minerals-tsxvdex-junior-explorer-targets-blind-copper-gold-porphyries-across-western-us-6553 Recording date: 17th July 2025 Almadex Minerals (TSXV:DEX) represents a unique proposition in the junior mining sector as a proven prospect generator with a systematic approach to early-stage exploration.

text:
Does anyone have thoughts or insights on Almadex Minerals?

Lately, I’ve been particularly interested in companies that have identified large lithocaps but have not yet released an MRE. My thinking is that these companies are often compelled to commit early to deeper drill holes, which can provide more definitive subsurface data rather than relying primarily on surface soil sampling.

Almadex appears to be focused almost exclusively on lithocap targets. CEO Morgan Poliquin is highly selective about the projects he believes exhibit the key characteristics of copper-gold porphyry and epithermal systems. Over the past few years, the company has steadily assembled land packages in the Western portion of the USA, primarily in Nevada and Arizona. If you search for Almadex Minerals on YouTube, you’ll find several recent interviews where he outlines their exploration philosophy and technical approach.

Unlike many junior explorers, Almadex carries no debt, holds approximately $20M in cash and bullion on its balance sheet, and hasn’t completed a financing since 2018. They also own six drill rigs, which they occasionally contract out to generate supplemental revenue. Of course, the cash and bullion will eventually be deployed, and future financings are likely inevitable, but their current financial position appears notably strong relative to peers.

That said, my only concern is:

The CEO often speaks very positively about certain projects as if they're the next big thing, only to immediately sideline them and enter into earn-in agreements with third parties (which he has addressed here: https://youtu.be/8obOpE6WOxM?t=738 and here https://youtu.be/8obOpE6WOxM?t=1814)

It led me to revisit Rick’s longstanding interest in the “prospect generator” model, and I spent some time reviewing his past comments on the topic. While the CEO is clearly familiar with the term, in this interview (https://youtu.be/8obOpE6WOxM?t=53) he seems offended having the company characterized that way.

Overall, I find the company intriguing. I appreciate how quickly they assess whether a land package meets their criteria and the discipline they appear to apply in their geological screening. Personally, I’d like to see more systematic drill data on specific projects, though that may simply come with time.

I’d appreciate any thoughts from those who have followed the company more closely.

It's great to see the continuity in the drill results isn't it Joe. Like Rick says, the drill results are becoming predictive. I still struggle with the question of high grade threshold and what specifically that will do for Hot Chili but I am pleased to see the grades maintained and close to surface.

I found this 'high grade' reference from a Mining.com article from 2017 which seems to shine favorably to these results which honestly, I am hoping get slightly higher. The article says, "COPPER: Anything over 100 metres and 1% copper equivalent or better is considered to be high-grade. For example, Serengeti Resources announced 119.6 metres of 0.9% copper equivalent (copper plus gold values added together) at depths from 180 to 300 metres. The stock then increased from $0.30 to $1.50 after those drilling results were reported.'

I think the next steps for me are to go back and review the start pit outline and grades for the old PFS. The recovers for the new results at La Verde are supposed to be comparable to the Costa Fuego metallurgy. They are something along the lines of Copper (Cu): 83%
Gold (Au): 53%
Molybdenum (Mo): 71%
Silver (Ag): 26%

So with a 0.2 gold equivlant added to the new grade drill results. I wonder about cut offs and recovery rates. 53% gold isn't what I would like to see for such low gold intercepts. Even the copper grades are on the lower end of solid recoveries. Not trying to be bearish, just thinking out loud here.

They are still waiting for the deeper intercepts to come back so hopefully the positive news continues and this resources continues to grow in size. It's already a heck of a mineral deposit they have on their hands.
The drilling is still ramping up though and I look forward to more extensions in and around the deposit.

The most recent PFS had Costa Fuego areas to have the following numbers, "The first 14 years should support the production of 95,000tpa copper and 48,000 ounces per annum gold from reserves now re-stated as 502Mt grading 0.37% copper, 0.10 grams per tonne gold, 0.49gpt silver, and 97 parts per million molybdenum."

Does anyone have any thoughts on Tag Oil (TAO:TSXV)?

Team: CHECK
CEO - Abby Badwi has had 3 previous successes, all directly related to the task at hand. Rally Energy sold for +$800M, working on heavy oil development in Egypt. Bankers Petroleum sold for +$800M developing Albanian oil assets by bringing Canadian expertise in unconventional well drilling. Kuwait Energy sold for +$800M focusing on developing a portfolio of oil and gas assets in MENA including Egypt.
Executive Team - various positions held by previous Bankers Petroleum team. They're getting the band back together.
Boar of Directors - Keith Hill, Rick's friend and former CEO of Meren/Africa Oil. He's a former Lundin Group of companies CEO. Has his foot in a range of frontier oil exploration companies.

Opportunity: CHECK
The company is primarily focused on exploring medium oil opportunities using Canadian unconventional drilling practices in Egypt. The country has a long history of oil production, and extensive infrastructure. Tag has bid and been granted licenses to explore 2 blocks. Both blocks have extensive data, 3D seismic, historical shut in past producing and exploration wells. For the 1st Block - BED1, the company has a 3rd party resource assessment stating that there are ~500M of Oil Initially in Place. Typical tight shale formation recovery is ~5% —> 25M barrels. The second concessions they won this past summer are much larger, with much larger potential resources.

Cost of the Test/Unanswered Questions:
For BED1, the company has previously drilled test wells and re-completions. They are targeting 2 additional wells and are planning a horizontal well. Additionally they have a field development plan in place for 18-20 wells. From what I can tell, the additional test wells will provide the data needed to confirm if they go ahead with the larger development plan. For the 2nd concessions, they are planning to do some stimulation via fracture to test the potential.

Financials/Structure: IFFY
The company is well funded ($4M in bank + $11.5M in new financing). This leaves them funded for the above tests, and will allow them to drill additional test/development wells. The biggest hurdle in my opinion is structure. The recent financing came with full warrants, exercisable a $0.13. Fully diluted new shares outstanding are almost double (so nearly 50% dilution). Since we're already aware of this, maybe it doesn't sting as much, but if I was an existing shareholder, I would probably want some clarity why they pursued so much equity at such a low share price. Maybe it was all that was on offer. Anyways… there is an additional $11.5M in funding if those warrants are exercised. Hopefully that structure doesn't lead to warrant stripping, or put an overhand on the stock price as people want to sell out of their stock when it gets above $0.13.

Overall:
I bought it. I like the potential upside, the existing infrastructure and resources. The cost of the test is relatively small compared with the potential reward. They don't seem to be facing much competition (no one else bid on the concession they won in the summer). Finally, the team in place now has had success together. Hoping they can repeat.
